related_questions.question: What are the different types of COVID vaccines?

text_blocks.snippet: In the United States, the two main types of COVID-19 vaccines currently recommended are mRNA vaccines (Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna) and a protein subunit vaccine (Novavax), according to the CDC. The Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) vaccine is no longer available in the U.S.

list.title: mRNA Vaccines:
list.snippet: These vaccines, like those from Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna, utilize mRNA to instruct cells to produce a harmless piece of the coronavirus (the spike protein). This triggers an immune response, teaching the body how to fight off the actual virus.

list.title: Protein Subunit Vaccine (Novavax):
list.snippet: This vaccine contains a harmless piece of the virus (the spike protein) and an adjuvant, which helps the immune system create a stronger response. The body then learns to recognize and fight the virus.
